findings.fp_reason: The flagged `is_admin()` check is not an authorization decision here. The callback only runs on Tutor course pages, skips enrolled users, loads the redirect target from stored course meta, casts it with `intval()`, resolves it through `get_permalink()`, and finally uses `wp_safe_redirect()`. No request parameter controls the redirect target in this entry point.

fp_evidence.defense: The redirect target is derived from stored post meta, cast to an integer, and normalized to a local permalink before redirection.

findings.fp_reason: The `is_admin()` check at line 259 only suppresses the redirect in admin screens; it does not gate privileged behavior. The actual redirect target comes from stored LearnDash course meta and is passed through `get_permalink()` before `wp_safe_redirect()`, so visitors cannot inject an arbitrary destination through this route.

fp_evidence.defense: The redirect uses a permalink generated from stored course metadata rather than request-controlled input.

findings.fp_reason: The analytics loader reads `version.json` and includes `class-bsf-analytics.php`, but the path originates from the hardcoded `CARTFLOWS_DIR . 'libraries/bsf-analytics'` value passed by `deactivation_survey_data_handler()`. I found no request-controlled or dynamic path input in the A5 slice, so the file-read/include sinks are limited to a fixed plugin directory.

fp_evidence.defense: The path handed to the analytics loader is a constant plugin-local directory, not attacker input.

findings.fp_reason: The `is_admin()` check at line 239 is reachable on admin requests, but the only side effect behind it is bootstrap insertion of a fixed list of CartFlows taxonomy terms (`landing`, `optin`, `checkout`, `thankyou`, `upsell`, `downsell`). The term names and slugs are fully static, so a low-privileged caller cannot influence what gets written or escalate privileges through this path.

fp_evidence.defense: The inserted terms come from a static in-code array rather than request data.

findings.fp_reason: The updater does call `update_option()` many times, but every branch is driven by the stored `cartflows-version` option and plugin constants during version migration. I did not find any request parameter or user-controlled key/value reaching these writes in the A5 slice, so this is maintenance logic rather than an attacker-driven arbitrary option update.

fp_evidence.defense: Migration decisions are based on a stored version string and plugin constants, not request data.

negative_findings.reason: Reviewed `modules/landing/classes/class-cartflows-landing-markup.php`, `modules/checkout/classes/class-cartflows-global-checkout.php`, `modules/flow/classes/class-cartflows-flow-post-type.php`, `modules/flow/classes/class-cartflows-step-post-type.php`, and `modules/thankyou/classes/class-cartflows-thankyou-markup.php`; the redirect targets are derived from `site_url()`, `get_permalink()`, or stored step metadata, with no request-controlled redirect target in this slice.

Reviewed `modules/optin/classes/class-cartflows-optin-markup.php`; the `$_POST['billing_email']` read in `remove_woo_actions()` only feeds `email_exists()` and checkout UI filters, and the same entry point does not reach a file, SQL, option, or code-execution sink.
